groups.title: The Musketeers
groups.explanation: These are the four friends of Dumas's novel The Three Musketeers.

groups.title: The four gospels
groups.explanation: The New Testament opens with these four gospels.

groups.title: Mountains of Greece
groups.explanation: Each is a mountain or range on the Greek mainland.

sources.excerpt: Although d'Artagnan is not able to join this elite corps immediately, he is befriended by three of the most formidable musketeers of the age – Athos, Porthos, and Aramis: "the three musketeers" or "the three inseparables" – and becomes involved in affairs of state and at court.
Mark was the first to be written, followed by Matthew and Luke, which forms a two-volume work with the Acts of the Apostles.
The author of John may have been aware of the synoptic gospels, and the gospel's historical context remains debated.
Mount Olympus has 52 peaks and deep gorges.
Parnassus has an abundance of trails for hiking in the three warm seasons.
The Pindus, Pindos or Pindhos is a mountain range located in Northern Greece and Southern Albania.
The Taygetus, Taugetus, Taygetos or Taÿgetus (Greek: Ταΰγετος, romanized: Taygetos) is a mountain range on the Peloponnese peninsula in Southern Greece.

editorNotes: Athos is the shared name, a musketeer and a holy mountain in northern Greece; the mountain group is already complete with Olympus, Parnassus, Pindus and Taygetus, so Athos joins the musketeers. Mark and John are ordinary first names, but the gospel group needs all four evangelists together.
